problemStatement.formal: f(k) = (1 + o(1)) · e/(e-1) · k, where f(k) is the minimal largest denominator in a (k+1)-term Egyptian fraction for 1
problemStatement.plain: The minimal largest denominator needed to write 1 as a sum of k+1 unit fractions is asymptotically e/(e-1) times k.
whyMatters: Resolves Erdős's question about Egyptian fraction complexity
The constant e/(e-1) ≈ 1.58 arises naturally from harmonic analysis
Connects number theory to analysis via exponential constants

proven: Lower and upper bounds on f(k)

currentState.focus: Zero sorries, one axiom (Martin 2000 asymptotic formula).
